hints: Focus on what happens when each chloride meets water, dissolving unchanged, hydrolysing gently, or reacting violently.
Remember NaCl is from a strong acid and strong base, so its solution stays neutral at about pH 7.
Compare SiCl4 which gives 4 moles of HCl per mole with AlCl3 where the highly charged Al3+ ion releases H+ ions, and decide if both can give a strongly acidic pH near 2.
walkthrough:
**Test-tube X with NaCl**

NaCl is an ionic salt of a Group 1 metal. It simply dissolves and does not hydrolyse.

$$\text{NaCl(s) + aq} \rightarrow \text{Na}^{+}\text{(aq)} + \text{Cl}^{-}\text{(aq)}$$
Neither ion reacts with water, so the solution stays neutral. Statement 1 is correct.

**Test-tube Y with SiCl4**

SiCl4 is a covalent tetrahedral chloride. It hydrolyses vigorously to give white fumes of HCl.

$$\text{SiCl}_{4}\text{(l)} + 2\text{H}_{2}\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{SiO}_{2}\text{(s)} + 4\text{HCl(aq)}$$
The strong acid HCl fully dissociates, so even a small amount gives a very low pH, about 2. Statement 2 is correct.

**Test-tube Z with AlCl3**

AlCl3 dissolves to give the hydrated ion $[\text{Al(H}_{2}\text{O)}_{6}]^{3+}$. The high charge density of $\text{Al}^{3+}$ polarises the O-H bonds in water.

$$[\text{Al(H}_{2}\text{O)}_{6}]^{3+} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O} \rightleftharpoons [\text{Al(H}_{2}\text{O)}_{5}\text{(OH)}]^{2+} + \text{H}_{3}\text{O}^{+}$$
This hydrolysis releases $\text{H}^{+}$ ions, making the solution distinctly acidic, typically pH 2 to 3. So pH 2 can be correct. Statement 3 is correct.

**Combine the conclusions**

Since statements 1, 2 and 3 can all be correct, the combination that includes all three is the right choice.

options.A: Correct because all three statements hold. X is neutral at pH 7, Y is strongly acidic from complete hydrolysis to HCl, and Z is acidic from hydrolysis of the Al3+ ion, which can give pH 2.
options.B: Incorrect because it includes 1 and 2 only and leaves out 3. Students choose this if they think AlCl3 gives a neutral solution like NaCl, forgetting that the small highly charged Al3+ ion hydrolyses to release H+.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes 2 and 3 only and leaves out 1. Students choose this if they think all chlorides hydrolyse to give acid, forgetting that NaCl from NaOH and HCl does not hydrolyse.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes 1 only. Students choose this if they think only NaCl dissolves normally and that covalent or Al chlorides do not affect pH, missing both hydrolysis reactions that produce acidity.
